transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-01-16
Start: 15:00 PST
Duration: 46 minutes (scheduled)
Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Daniel Soto (Redwood Product), Mark Rivers (CTO, Bluemeridian), Sara Patel (Eng Manager), Omar Haddad (Security), Jin Park (Platform)

Summary: quick console demo focusing on key topology (org vs project keys), rate-sculpting policies, and a proposed pilot on Redwood Dedicated. Customer concerned about latency/cost tradeoffs, VPC/KMS for PHI, and pilot metrics.

Topics: rate limiting, quotas, org/project key mapping, burst handling, fairshare, dedicated capacity pilot, security/compliance ask

Transcript:
[00:00] Alex Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick intros, I'm Alex, AE on the account. Priya is our SE, she'll run the console demo and show the key mapping flows.
[00:14] Mark Rivers: Hi all, Mark here. We're trying to understand how Redwood can replace part of our inference stack for patient-facing summarization without blowing budget.
[00:22] Sara Patel: Sara - platform, we'll own the keys and routing. main questions are: do we pin tenants to hardware, how do quotas look, and can we keep traffic inside our VPC?
[00:35] Priya Nair: Great, those are exactly the things we'll cover. quick callout - we have a couple of options: Hosted API for fastest onramp, Dedicated pools for predictable throughput, and Private (VPC) for stricter isolation. we can mix and match.
[00:50] Jin Park: Is Private fully on-prem or VPC-peered? our security team is picky about data exfil.
[00:58] Priya Nair: We do both; for Bluemeridian I'd recommend Redwood Private with VPC peering or our on-prem package if you need air gap. KMS/HSM integration is supported, and we'll show where that lives in the console.
[01:12] Mark Rivers: OK. on the rate stuff, we're worried about noisy tenants - we have a couple of partners that spike and ruin latency for everyone. how do you do fairshare?
[01:22] Priya Nair: We have org and project key hierarchies. Org keys are top-level and allow you to apply global quotas and routing policies. Project keys can be scoped per product/team. Then we have a rate-sculpting layer - think of it as lanes with backpressure. we can do guaranteed lanes for critical endpoints and best-effort lanes for bulk embeddings.
[01:40] Speaker 1: um huh, yeah
[01:44] Alex Chen: quick demo - opening the Console. (typing noises) Sorry, little lag. so here is the Key Topology page. you can see our example org called "Bluemeridian-org" and we have projects underneath like "patient-summaries" and "partner-ingest".
[02:05] Priya Nair: i'll click into project-level quotas. notice you can set concurrency quotas, token-rate limits, and burst tokens. the burst tokens use a leaky-bucket algorithm so short spikes are absorbed but sustained spikes get shaped.
[02:22] Sara Patel: leaky-bucket vs token-bucket? our infra folks asked.
[02:26] Priya Nair: it's essentially a token-bucket implementation with a controllable refill rate; we expose the knobs as Window rate and Burst capacity. apologies if earlier i said leaky-bucket, sometimes the docs mix the terms.
[02:37] Mark Rivers: can we set per-route SLOs and have requests fall back to a cheaper model if the primary is saturated?
[02:44] Priya Nair: yes - policy chains. you can configure a primary model and then a fallback variant. the routing policy evaluates latency targets, cost thresholds, and capacity. if primary can't meet the latency SLO, request auto-fails over to a compatible quantized variant.
[02:58] Jin Park: that fallback - does it preserve KV cache or will cold start blow latency?
[03:03] Priya Nair: fallbacks can be configured to prefer models that share the same KV cache topology when possible, but if you switch architectures it's cold. we also have prefix caching for common prompts which reduces cold-start impact.
[03:17] Alex Chen: bringing it back to multi-tenant fairness - here's our FairShare policy editor. you can weight projects, set min-guarantees, and configure burst fences. for example, if "partner-ingest" exceeds its burst fence we'll throttle it to steady-state rate and protect "patient-summaries" lanes.
[03:36] Sara Patel: how are weights calculated across orgs? do we get per-org isolation?
[03:41] Priya Nair: yes, you can apply org-level isolation slices. we expose a slice allocator where you can divide cluster capacity by org, then within org you can further slice by project. slices support sticky routing so long-lived sessions can stay on the same pool which helps KV cache hits.
[03:58] Mark Rivers: sticky routing seems useful for sessionized summarization. but what about billing - if we pin sticky routing, does that increase cost?
[04:05] Daniel Soto: it can, because pinning affects statistical multiplexing. we can model the TCO - that's why we'll share the TCO spreadsheet showing tradeoffs between latency SLO and cost.
[04:15] Speaker 2: uh-huh
[04:18] Priya Nair: moving on - i'll show a sample policy. (clicks) This policy sets a concurrency cap of 50 tokens/sec for patient-summaries, gives partner-ingest a weight of 0.2, and reserves 20% of capacity for the org's critical lanes. Burst tokens set to 1000 for short spikes.
[04:37] Jin Park: can we enforce quotas by endpoint path not just key? e.g., /summaries/api/v2 vs /batch-embed?
[04:44] Priya Nair: yes, route-level policies are supported. in the console you can bind a policy to a route, an API key, or a tag. so path-based enforcement is straightforward.
[04:54] Mark Rivers: good. uptime and SLOs - what's Redwood Dedicated SLA for latency percentiles?
[04:59] Alex Chen: Dedicated customers get latency SLOs per model class, e.g., 99th pct target of X ms on specific configs. the exact numbers depend on the committed pool size and model variant. we'll include the SLA doc with the security pack.
[05:12] Omar Haddad: Security - we need SOC2, ISO, SAML/SSO, audit logs, and KMS where customer controls key. also data residency for EU patients. do you support customer-managed KMS?
[05:25] Priya Nair: yes to SAML/SSO and audit logs. we integrate with customer KMS for Private deployments; for Hosted there is a managed option but we can do a hybrid for key wrapping. we'll send the SOC2 and encryption docs.
[05:35] Mark Rivers: and egress? we need to ensure model outputs never leave our VPC for certain endpoints.
[05:41] Priya Nair: for those endpoints you can put them on the Private deployment or on-prem package so traffic never traverses Redwood public network; logs can be forwarded to your SIEM via secure collectors.
[05:52] Speaker 3: mm-hmm
[05:55] Alex Chen: back to quotas - here's an advanced scenario: auto-scale with backpressure. if a tenant spikes we'll first try bursting, then if sustained we activate backpressure which drops or delays lower-priority lanes based on policy. you can set backpressure thresholds in tokens/sec and a TTL for the backpressure state.
[06:18] Sara Patel: can the system notify us and open a PagerDuty when backpressure is triggered? we need observability hooks.
[06:24] Priya Nair: yes, Console integrates with webhook alerts, PagerDuty, and you get token-level breakdowns. we'll demo the dashboard panels briefly.
[06:33] Alex Chen: quick note - our Optimize tool can run experiments to find an efficient quantization level and batching config given your latency distribution. we can run that as part of the pilot.
[06:46] Jin Park: how intrusive is Optimize? does it touch model weights?
[06:50] Daniel Soto: Optimize is a config-time tool - it recommends quantization and batching and we validate on your workload; we don't change weights without approval. it generates profiles and predicted token throughput and cost.
[07:05] Alex Chen: demo continues - switching to Observability > Billing breakdown. here you get per-route token cost and an incremental cost curve for tail latency. customers often use this view to set cost caps per project.
[07:20] Mark Rivers: Could we limit total spend per project and block calls once the budget is exhausted?
[07:25] Priya Nair: yes, there's a hard quota option that returns 429s when exceeded, plus soft quotas that alert and start throttling. you can also configure debt windows so the system allows short overspend before enforcement.
[07:39] Speaker 1: hmm
[07:41] Mark Rivers: one of our constraints is we use a proprietary reranker that needs to run on a GPU for latency. can we route certain routes to dedicated pools that have pinned GPUs?
[07:53] Priya Nair: absolutely. dedicated pools support node selectors by hardware type and you can pin routes to pool IDs. routing policy allows you to prefer dedicated pools for high-priority paths.
[08:03] Sara Patel: and if dedicated pool is saturated does Redwood automatically fallback to hosted pool?
[08:09] Priya Nair: there's an automatic fallback policy you can enable - typically you'd set cost and security constraints; if fallback is allowed, requests route to a compatible hosted variant, otherwise requests queue or return 503 depending on policy.
[08:22] Jin Park: we will need detailed benchmark numbers. can you run a short throughput test against our sample payloads?
[08:27] Alex Chen: yes, that's part of the pilot. priya will set up a two-week pilot config with load harness and we'll run the same trace you provide.
[08:35] Mark Rivers: timeline: decision by end of Feb. pilot needs to be done before we commit.
[08:40] Alex Chen: sounds good. we'll aim to start pilot next week pending security ok.
[08:45] Speaker 2: okay
[08:48] Priya Nair: quick callout - i'll show a failure scenario: if partner-ingest keeps spiking, the FairFence will kick in at 90% of burst capacity, we cut partner throughput to steady-share and direct remaining capacity to patient-summaries. here's the logs view where you see throttled requests and the policy eval trace.
[09:10] Sara Patel: is the policy eval deterministic? can we replay it for an audit?
[09:15] Priya Nair: yes, we keep policy evaluation traces and they can be exported. good for debug and for compliance.
[09:24] Alex Chen: quick QA: any blockers on security?
[09:28] Omar Haddad: KMS integration details, encryption-at-rest proof, and where logs are stored. also need to know whether Redwood's support org can be restricted for access to logs.
[09:40] Priya Nair: we can restrict support access and integrate with customer KMS in Private. we'll send the specifics.
[09:47] Mark Rivers: another question - how do you handle API keys rotation and secret management across projects?
[09:53] Priya Nair: we support automated key rotation, project-level RBAC, and tokens with TTLs. keys can be scoped to routes and namespaces.
[10:02] Jin Park: if we use project keys heavily, is there an explosion of metadata and does it affect performance?
[10:07] Daniel Soto: we've optimized the routing table; millions of keys are supported. the lookup performance is O(1) in our router and we shard the metadata.
[10:17] Speaker 3: wow
[10:20] Priya Nair: demo - now showing how to define a route policy that ties path, allowed keys, and SLO. (clicks) you can then attach a rollout policy - canary % and automatic rollback if latency regresses.
[10:36] Sara Patel: automatic rollback - what's the window and what metrics trigger rollback?
[10:40] Priya Nair: you configure the evaluation window (e.g., 5m) and trigger thresholds for p95/p99 latency and error rate. Rollback is automatic if thresholds exceeded for consecutive windows.
[10:51] Alex Chen: ok will recap and close in a few. any final questions?
[10:56] Mark Rivers: Are there any examples of customers with similar PHI constraints?
[11:01] Alex Chen: yes, we have healthcare customers using Private deployments. we'll anonymize reference and include contact if you want.
[11:08] Sara Patel: one more - do you support per-token censoring or redaction before logs leave our VPC?
[11:14] Priya Nair: we support redaction hooks and pre-log transforms in Private; logs can be stored in your object store via connectors.
[11:23] Alex Chen: recap of next steps: share pricing/TCO, security docs, pilot config, and traffic profile. priya will provision pilot. we'll reconvene after pilot baseline.
[11:34] Mark Rivers: thanks everyone, appreciate the walkthrough.
[11:36] Alex Chen: thanks all, we'll follow up over email.

End of transcript.
